answers.core:
`ResourcePath` is supposed to be a built-in engine type that needs editor integration.


`@export var monsters: Dictionary[String, Resource]`
* Loading the parent .tres or .tscn automatically loads all referenced resources.
This is undesirable for large datasets (e.g., RPG databases, item registries, monster definitions).

* There is no lazy loading.

* There is no control over when or how referenced resources are loaded.

`@export var monsters: Dictionary[String, String]  # "res://monsters/slime.tres"`
This has the following drawbacks:

* No editor integration.
* No drag‑and‑drop.
* No type safety.
* No automatic path updates when files are moved.
* No inline editing of the referenced resource.
answers.workaround: As described, you can store plain strings or UIDs(which is just a string as well). The former breaks when files are moved around, the latter is unreadable. Both of these solutions do not have a editor integration (no thumbnails, no in-editor editing, no drag/drop )

title: ResourcePath as an in-between plain String and a Resource
